issues.legal_issue: A further revision under the general civil procedure code is unavailable after the revision route provided by a rent-control statute has been used and the statute makes the matter final subject to that route.
material_facts: The eviction proceeding was brought under a rent-control statute that provided an appeal and a designated revision from the appellate authority’s decision.
The appellate authority was a subordinate judge, so the statutory revision lay to the district court.
After the district court dismissed the statutory revision, the landlord sought a further revision in the High Court under the general civil procedure code.
The High Court entertained that further revision, set aside the decisions below, and ordered eviction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had no jurisdiction to interfere under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure; its judgment and order were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18(5) and 20 of the Kerala Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1965, a decision is final and cannot be called in question except through the revision provided by section 20. Read together, those provisions exclude a second revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure after the designated statutory revision has been decided. The statutory scheme provides its own tier of courts and requires finality; it does not contemplate two revisions. The Court relied on Kydd v. Watch Committee of City of Liverpool, South Asia Industries Private Ltd. v. S.B. Sarup Singh and Others, and Vishesh Kumar v. Shanti Prasad; distinguished Maung Ba Thaw and Another—Insolvents v. Ma Pin; approved Kurien v. Chacko; and overruled Ouseph Vareed v. Mary.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: A party brought an eviction proceeding under a statute governing rent-controlled premises.
predicates.statute_limits_challenge_to_designated_r: The governing statute makes the decision final subject to a specified revision and does not provide for a further revision after that route.
predicates.designated_revision_already_decided: The party pursued the specified revision, and the reviewing court decided it.
predicates.further_challenge_sought_under_general_c: After the specified revision was decided, a party sought another revision under the general civil procedure code.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is governed by a statute that confines further challenge to a specified revision, and that revision has already been decided, a party cannot obtain another revision under the general civil procedure code.

issues.legal_issue: A matter cannot be remitted for consideration as a constitutional supervisory petition merely because a revision under the general civil procedure code is unavailable.
material_facts: After the High Court’s revision under the general civil procedure code was held unavailable, the landlord asked that the matter be remitted for consideration as a petition invoking the High Court’s constitutional supervisory power.
The Court declined that request, distinguishing the two procedures and stating that it was not deciding the scope of the High Court’s constitutional powers.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to remit the case for consideration as a constitutional supervisory petition, while leaving the scope of that constitutional power undecided.
issues.legal_principle: A petition under Article 227 of the Constitution and a revision under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure are distinct procedures and are not interchangeable. The Court did not decide the scope of the High Court’s powers under Article 227.

predicates.appeal_from_rent_control_proceeding: A party appealed after proceedings under a statute governing rent-controlled premises.
predicates.further_general_civil_revision_unavailab: The statutory route for review had been used, and the governing scheme did not permit another revision under the general civil procedure code.
predicates.party_requests_remittal_for_constitution: A party asked the court to remit the matter for consideration under the High Court’s constitutional supervisory power.

issues.definition: When a further civil revision is unavailable in an appeal arising from a rent-control proceeding, a request to remit the matter for constitutional supervision is denied if the court treats the two procedures as distinct and non-interchangeable.
